data: Writing in Mathematics and Quantitative Sciences

Writing and communicating mathematical ideas are becoming more and more important to practitioners of Mathematics and mathematically oriented sciences. While Mathematics is concerned with theorems and proofs, disciplines such as Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Economics, and Data Science additionally employ mathematical formalism for modeling and mathematical statistics for data analysis. Writing and communication in these disciplines take the form of research publications as well as writing in public forums in accessible language. This course explores writing and communicating mathematical knowledge in two distinct but related registers: technical and non-technical (specifically, journalistic) writing. The first register discusses how to convey mathematical ideas in the form of proofs, model derivations, and statistical analysis to a technically trained audience, while the second register explores how science journalists disseminate these ideas to a wider readership. In this course, the students will read exemplary pieces of academic and journalistic mathematical writing to derive principles of effective communication and implement the same in their
 own writing.
